To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the reduced electric quadrupole transition probabilities B(E 2) and partial half-lifes T 1/2(E 2) for various levels in 111,113 Cd, as well as the E2/Ml mixing ratios for various transitions from these levels.
the first 2+ levels in the even-even isotopes of natural cadmium, /sup 110, 112, 114, 116/Cd were Coulombs excited with 2--4.2MeV protons.
we have studied the low-lying positive parity states in /sup 110,111,112,113/Cd using Coulomb excitation with protons and measured the reduced E2 transition rates and partial half-lifes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear structure and the development of nuclear instrumentation.
the development of a new type of neutron detector for use in the detection of neutrons from a pulsed spallation neutron source.
the development of a new method for the determination of trace amounts of plutonium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results are not consistent with the theoretical predictions.
the present work has established a new and improved experimental data base for the positive parity levels in natural cadmium isotopes.

the results obtained in this work are in excellent agreement with the theoretical calculations of the E2 transition strengths and gamma-ray angular distributions, but are in disagreement with the theoretical calculations on the level energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present work is a continuation of the work on the study of the structure of Cd isotopes through the Coulomb excitation technique.
the present work is a continuation of a study of the low-lying states of the odd-mass cadmium isotopes.

we have Coulomb-excited the first 2 + states in the even-even Cd isotopes, and the 3/2 + states in /sup 112,114,Cd and the 5/2 + state in /sup 116/Cd, and also the 3/1/2 + states of /sup 112-116/Cd and the 3- state of /sup 114/Cd.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 700, 755, 855, and 1021 keV levels in 111Cd have a spin of (3/ 2)+ and the 1130 keV level has a spin of ( 5/2)+.
the 1130 keV level in 111 Cd has been Coulomb excited for the first time with protons, and has been assigned a (5/2)+ spin value.

the E2 transition probabilities of the levels in /111,113/Cad are much larger than the values predicted by shell model calculations, and are comparable to the E2 transition probability of 2/sup +/-/ states in the neighboring nuclei.
